meta.title: AI Governance Radar
meta.geographic_scope: 193 UN members + State of Palestine + Holy See
meta.geography_note: The map is a vector map drawn in the browser with d3-geo in the Equal Earth projection from TopoJSON country shapes, so it stays sharp at every zoom level: scroll, pinch or the + / − buttons zoom, dragging pans, and the reset button returns to the world view. The September 2026 UN Correct the Map resolution encourages Equal Earth and other equal-area projections. Country shapes are simplified Natural Earth 1:10m Admin-0 Countries and the land outline beneath them is Natural Earth 1:50m; neither is official UN boundary data, and the boundaries shown do not imply any position on territorial status. All 195 countries are represented. Filters by governance category, document type, issuing organisation and record status highlight the countries with at least one matching national document and dim the rest; an optional checkbox also counts regional instruments that apply to a country (such as the EU AI Act). Selecting an international body (EU, GCC, AU, ASEAN, Council of Europe, UNESCO, OECD, ICESCO, ALECSO, G7, G20) highlights its member countries; for the Council of Europe, CETS 225 ratifications, CETS 225 signatures, Convention 108 parties and other member states are shown in separate shades, and for the OECD, members and the non-member countries adhering to its AI Recommendation are shown separately. Each country has its own page; its counts and charts group instruments as binding or mandatory (laws, regulations, treaties and policies mandatory within their scope), non-binding (strategies, guidelines, guidance, codes and opinions) and drafts (consultation drafts). Document lists can be sorted newest first (the default), by legal weight (binding law, treaty, regulation, mandatory policy, guidance, strategy, draft) or grouped by category. The Updates tab lists the government actions dated within the last 30 days across all countries by default (60 days, 90 days, all dates or upcoming dates can be selected; the period is counted from the reader's current date), newest first, filterable by country and by type (new, revised, applied). The whole dataset or a single country can be exported as CSV or JSON. Flags are embedded SVG images from the MIT-licensed flag-icons collection, version 7.5.0.
meta.analysis_note: The Analysis page (/analysis/) charts the whole snapshot and the Timeline page (/timeline/) places every dated instrument on one time axis. Both count officially published documents found by this radar, grouped as binding or mandatory (laws, regulations, treaties and policies mandatory within their scope), non-binding (strategies, guidelines, guidance, codes and opinions) and drafts (consultation drafts); leads are not counted. Counts do not measure the quality or strength of a country's AI governance. The region charts default to national-level instruments, with a switch to add state/provincial and local ones; subnational coverage is deeper for the United States, Canada, Australia, Brazil, India and China, so totals that include it are not comparable across regions. Regional instruments (such as the EU AI Act) are counted once for the body that issued them, not for each member state, which lowers counts for EU members. Recent years are better represented: newer documents are more often online, so growth since 2023 is partly a discovery effect. On the adoption curve, instruments first published before 2016 (mostly data-protection, copyright and sector laws) are dated by the amendment or provision that made them relevant to AI where the record states it, on both the any-instrument and the binding-or-mandatory lines; those without such a date are left off both lines and listed for a later data pass. The national-strategy line uses publication dates. Convention 108 parties are counted only where the national ratification or accession act was found, so the count is lower than the Council of Europe Treaty Office's list. Issuer types come from each record's authority type; records without one are shown as unclassified. Every chart has a table view and a CSV download, and a reconciliation table ties the chart totals to the export.
meta.evidence_policy: Only located official sources are listed. Source location is distinguished from document-level metadata review. Null values mean unverified; missing records do not establish absence.
meta.regional_policy: EU records stored once and inherited by 27 Member States. Other regional layers browsable without assumed national adoption.
meta.source_check_policy: Automated GET checks assess accessibility only, not correctness or current legal status.
meta.change_policy: Every change is logged as a dated event. World events (published, revised, consultation, adopted, applied, superseded, repealed) record government actions; radar events (added, corrected, removed, link) record changes to this database. Automatically detected events stay marked 'needs review' until confirmed against the official source.
